summary:
H.R. 8580, the "Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025," is a regular appropriations bill making discretionary and mandatory appropriations for FY 2025 (fiscal year ending September 30, 2025) across four titles. It passed the House June 5, 2024, and was placed on the Senate calendar (PCS) September 12, 2024. The text contains numerous placeholder amendments (e.g., "(increased by $X)(reduced by $X)") reflecting floor-amendment artifacts that net to zero.

**Title I – Department of Defense (Military Construction).** Appropriates funds by component for acquisition and construction of military facilities as authorized by law, including Army ($2,217,757,000), Navy/Marine Corps ($4,332,414,000), Air Force ($3,268,276,000), and Defense-Wide ($3,500,083,000, with transfer authority), each available until September 30, 2029, with caps on planning/design funds subject to Secretarial override and congressional notification. Additional appropriations fund the National Guard and Reserve components (per chapter 1803, title 10), the NATO Security Investment Program (10 U.S.C. 2806), the DoD Base Closure Account (10 U.S.C. 2687 note), family housing accounts, and the Family Housing/Unaccompanied Housing Improvement Funds (10 U.S.C. 2883). Administrative provisions (Secs. 101–133) impose standard restrictions: cost-plus contract approval thresholds, American-steel and U.S.-contractor preferences, notification requirements, reprogramming per DoD FMR 7000.14-R, and prohibitions on funds for closure/realignment of Naval Station Guantanamo Bay (Sec. 133). Several additional appropriations (Secs. 124, 128–132) are conditioned on prior authorization and submission/approval of expenditure plans.

**Title II – Department of Veterans Affairs.** Provides current-year and advance (FY 2026) appropriations for mandatory benefit accounts (Compensation and Pensions; Readjustment Benefits; Insurance) and loan accounts, plus discretionary appropriations for VBA operations, VHA Medical Services ($75,039,000,000), Medical Community Care, Medical Support and Compliance, Medical Facilities, research, National Cemetery Administration, IT Systems, the Electronic Health Record system ($894,000,000, with 25% withheld until July 1, 2025 pending certifications), construction accounts, and the Cost of War Toxic Exposures Fund ($22,800,000,000). Administrative provisions (Secs. 201–261) grant conditional transfer authority (subject to congressional approval), and impose policy riders including prohibitions on abortion funding (Sec. 255, with rape/incest/life exceptions), gender-affirming surgical/hormone care (Sec. 256), phase-out of canine/feline/primate research by March 9, 2026 (Sec. 246), and SSN authentication discontinuance (Sec. 236, superseding P.L. 117-328 §237). Sec. 219 repeals section 220 of Title II of division A of P.L. 118-42.

**Title III – Related Agencies.** Funds the American Battle Monuments Commission, the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims ($47,200,000), Army cemeterial expenses (Arlington), and the Armed Forces Retirement Home.

**Title IV – General Provisions (Secs. 401–430).** Government-wide riders prohibit funds for implementing enumerated Executive Orders (Secs. 414, 419, 420), diversity/equity/inclusion activities (Sec. 417), "Critical Race Theory" (Sec. 415), Guantanamo detainee transfers (Sec. 412), and certain PRC-linked IT procurement (Sec. 421). Sec. 401 restricts availability to the current fiscal year absent express provision.
